patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents to the urgent care clinic complaining of epigastric discomfort and cramping pain for the past 2 hours. She reports experiencing similar pain episodes in the past, mostly post-meals, which often subside several hours after eating. This has led her to avoid eating, resulting in weight loss over the past couple of months. She has a habit of smoking and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her past medical history is insignificant except for chronic knee pain, for which she takes over-the-counter painkillers.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Chronic knee pain treated with over-the-counter painkillers. No other significant medical history.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Patient denies any changes in bowel or urinary habits, no nausea or vomiting reported.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with epigastric discomfort and cramping pain.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “I’ve had epigastric discomfort and cramping pain for about two hours now, and it feels similar to episodes I’ve had before—usually after meals. The pain often gets better a few hours after eating, but it’s made me avoid eating and I’ve lost some weight over the past couple of months.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any joint swelling—just my usual knee pain that I manage with over-the-counter painkillers.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp. The issue is mainly the epigastric discomfort and cramping that tends to come on after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a feeling of itchiness anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any itching or itchiness anywhere on my body.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble raising your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “No trouble raising my arms above my head—I can lift them fully without any pain or weakness.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any loss of vision or any eye symptoms that come without pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had a fever or felt extremely hot like that, and I haven’t been dizzy—I’ve just been dealing with the epigastric discomfort and cramping pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I have been feeling a bit stressed, mainly because the pain keeps coming back after meals and I’ve been avoiding eating, but I don’t feel overwhelmed all the time—just more anxious about it since it’s affected my eating and weight.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate. My symptoms have been centered on the epigastric discomfort and cramping pain after meals.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any chills. It’s mainly been the epigastric discomfort and cramping pain after meals, and it has helped some after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breasts—nothing that feels fixed or doesn’t move.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes—mostly it’s centered in the upper abdomen between my ribs (epigastric area), and I also feel cramping there rather than pain in my back. It seems to come on after meals and then gradually improves over a few hours.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have calf pain when I walk, and it doesn’t go away with rest—I haven’t noticed anything like that. My discomfort has been specifically in my upper abdomen between my ribs, and it tends to come after eating and ease over a few hours.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual. My main issue is still the epigastric discomfort and cramping that tends to come on after meals and then improves over a few hours.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have any difficulty moving my arms up or across my body—I can lift and move them normally without pain or weakness.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your joints feel sore or stiff after doing the same activity repeatedly, like after a long day of typing, lifting, or other repetitive motions?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any joint soreness or stiffness after repetitive activities—my only ongoing discomfort is my usual knee pain. My current problem is mainly the epigastric cramping and discomfort that starts after meals and then eases over a few hours.”
